pattern-selector.why: the runner is a deliberate design choice: a single small command module / Gateway over path resolution and a timed, shell-free subprocess, not a new abstraction and not a full esk CLI for one use.
pattern-selector.what: chose no GoF object pattern; always-on/run-check.mjs is a plain command module matching scripts/compare-gate-runs.mjs, with the pattern-decision record (forces, cost of deferring, rejected options) recorded in ADR-0096.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: the decision (ship a fail-closed runner plus a convention, not docs-only and not a full CLI) is recorded in the same change as the code.
architectural-decision-records.what: added docs/adr/0096-checker-runner-fail-closed.md (context, three considered options, decision, consequences with honest limits) and a CHANGELOG entry; updated the ADR skill to run its checker through the runner.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the three issue behaviors (a selected skill that cannot load blocks; a missing checker blocks the finish; a timed-out checker counts as a failure) are enumerated as scenarios, stored, logged, and run on the harness.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added features/always-on/skills-formula-every-task.feature and skills-apply-every-task.feature with step defs driving the real run-check.mjs; regenerated the datastore; appended the coverage log.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the runner's behavior is proven at the lowest layer that can catch the bug: unit/integration tests that spawn the real script, not a browser or a stand-in.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/run-check.test.mjs: resolution, fail-closed blocks (missing skill, missing checker, timeout, signal-kill), the pass and checker-failed paths, name safety, and a verbose-output maxBuffer case.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the runner is itself a check (it decides pass/block), so it must be proven able to fail: its tests flip when the runner is neutralized.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: test/run-check.test.mjs is discriminating: against a no-op run-check (always exit 0), 15 of 16 cases fail; the one that still passes is the explicitly-labeled shell-pipe characterization that never invokes run-check.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the runner enforces evidence discipline in code (no stand-in judgment counts; a missing or timed-out checker is a block, not an assumed pass), and the ADR carries evidence states and named limits.
skeptical-audit.what: the ADR states each claim's evidence state and the honest limits (reports a block but does not stop a turn; a .sh checker needs bash); the runner refuses to let a missing/unstartable/timed-out checker read as a pass.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the runner resolves a filesystem path from caller-supplied names and spawns a subprocess, so it is threat-modeled against path traversal and command injection.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: skill and script names are validated (only [A-Za-z0-9._-], no '..', no path separators) before any filesystem access, so resolution cannot escape a skills root; the checker is spawned with no shell (args array), so neither the path nor pass-through args are shell-interpreted; both controls are covered by test/run-check.test.mjs.
quotes: Each per-sheet file states the real attack the control stops

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review ran on the diff before this receipt; it returned PASS with no four-questions violation and no fail-closed hole, and raised non-blocking notes that were addressed.
judge-arch.what: dispatched the four-questions review to a general-purpose subagent; it traced every exit path (no false-pass path); fixed its notes - added signal-kill and verbose-output tests, removed a dead ternary, wrapped the inline statSync, raised maxBuffer with an ENOBUFS block; recorded in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no new system or data architecture, schema, service, or scaling surface; the boundary, ownership, dependency, and error-handling review for this small single-owner utility is carried by judge-arch (applied) and the design by pattern-selector (applied).

arch-encode.why: no new greppable arch-gate rule was encoded; the fix is a runtime fail-closed mechanism plus a discriminating test, not a static lint over source that a rule could express.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, release, rollout, cutover, migration, or feature flag; nothing about what runs in production changes.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, alert, or on-call surface; a local CLI utility invoked by an agent or a future finish-check hook.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, consent, retention, audit log, backup, or data migration; the runner resolves and runs local scripts only.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no UI; a command-line utility with no rendered interface.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser- or device-facing code; a Node CLI script.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing UI; the runner's developer-facing CLI messages follow the repo's existing checker-message style (a clear cause plus the fix to apply).
